items.author: xaskasdf
items.descZh: 作者在浏览电子游戏相关资料时，意外获得了一份泄露的《辛普森一家：撞击与奔跑》游戏源码，并对其进行了修复，主要解决了在 Windows 11 宽屏环境下运行时的音频故障、内存泄漏、安全漏洞以及强制信箱模式（letterbox）等兼容性问题。这是一则非正式发布的民间修复帖，作者以"fix some pretty bad issues"轻描淡写地概括了多项底层修复工作，但未提供具体的性能数据或测试指标，也未说明分发渠道或后续维护计划，因此内容更像是个人的技术修补分享，而非正式的产品发布公告。适用人群仅限于希望在现代宽屏系统中重温这款经典老游戏的怀旧玩家和模组爱好者，需注意该资源来源为泄露源码，存在一定的法律与安全风险。

items.author: ringlochid
items.descZh: ImageSage 是一款面向 Windows 10/11 的本地化、私密 AI 照片管理应用，主打以自然语言搜索查找图片。其核心功能包括：单一搜索框即可理解图片视觉内容（visual meaning）、通过设备端 OCR 识别图中文字（text in images），以及按文件名与路径（name & path）过滤定位照片。亮点方面，"Magic Rename" 功能可对选中图片批量建议简洁文件名，用户可在应用前逐条审阅、编辑并确认，所有重命名操作均在本地完成，且索引过程不会移动原图（indexing never moves originals on its own），同时支持在搜索结果内直接对原文件执行移动、复制、删除或原地操作（act in place）。整个应用采用端侧 AI 推理（on-device AI），无需账号注册，强调"Private by design"的隐私优先设计理念。该工具特别适合拥有大量本地照片库、想通过图像内容或图中文字快速检索、又不愿将数据上传云端的 Windows 用户。

items.descZh: 为帮助孩子建立独立的网络身份，作者从假词生成器中挑选外观最佳的虚构词汇，并通过域名注册商进行搜索，最终为孩子注册个性化定制域名，展现了一种富有创意且成本可控的网络身份管理方式。整个过程强调去重和手动筛选，以确保域名的独特性与可用性。亮点在于借助免费工具生成候选词，再结合传统注册查询，有效避免重名问题并提升注册成功率。具体性能数据未在原文中提及。该方案适合希望为孩子或家庭成员打造独立网络身份、注重隐私保护与个性化表达的用户，尤其适用于家长群体。

items.author: vamgan
items.descZh: 随着 AI 编码代理(如 Claude Code、Codex)在团队中大规模落地,代码评审中反复出现的相同问题(命名规范、错误处理、日志格式等)成为最消耗审查者精力的痛点。reviewtorule 正是为解决"评审一次就永远记住"这一场景而设计的开源工具,作为 Claude Code 插件或跨平台技能(支持 Codex 等)安装,无需独立 CLI、npm 包或额外认证。它能从 GitHub、GitLab、Bitbucket、Gerrit、Azure Repos 等任意平台拉取已被接受的评审意见及其修订 diff,经确定性助手处理后,将反馈沉淀为带作用域(scope)的仓库级长期记忆规则文件。运行时仅需 Node.js 24+ 与 Git,内置 Vitest 测试与 ESLint/Prettier 质量门禁,可作为 PR 检查自动校验未来是否违反既有规则。典型适用场景包括:大型团队统一编码风格、新成员快速对齐项目惯例、消除跨项目中反复出现的低级评审意见,以及让 AI 代理在每次新会话中自动遵循历史评审沉淀的工程准则。
items.quote: 审阅者发现一次，未来每次审阅都会记住。

items.author: neehao
items.descZh: Indicate 是 inrolls 团队开源的印地语系语言转写工具，托管在 GitHub 上，已获得 17 颗 Star、2 次 Fork，拥有 166 次提交记录，活跃度较高。其核心功能是利用 PyTorch 传统模型与大型语言模型（LLM）实现印度语系语言与英语之间的高质量双向转写，覆盖印地语、泰米尔语、泰卢固语、孟加拉语、古吉拉特语等 12 种以上语言，并能自动检测源文字脚本。亮点在于可组合的后端架构，用户可按任意顺序串联词典表、本地模型和 LLM；支持结构化 JSON 输出、批量处理与进度跟踪，并具备生产级的原子写入与备份机制，安装时仅需 Python 3.13+ 即可通过 pip install indicate 一键部署，PyTorch 权重首次从 Hugging Face 下载后即可完全离线运行。该工具特别适合需要处理印度多语种姓名、地名或大规模文本转写的开发者与数据团队，可应用于选举名册清洗、跨语言搜索索引、NLP 数据预处理以及本地化翻译等场景。
items.quote: Indicate 使用传统 PyTorch 模型和最先进的 LLM(大语言模型)，提供印度语言与英语之间的高质量音译。

items.title: Show HN: 58% US County fail PDF Accessibility
items.desc: description: US counties must make their PDFs accessible by 26 April 2027. We drew a random sample of 100 US counties, harvested 941 documents from their public portals, and found 58.1% have no tag tree at all meaning a screen reader gets no headings, no reading order, and no table structure. title: The State of US County PDF Accessibility 2026 image: https://accesslumens.com/opengraphimage.png 58.1% Have no tag tree 547 of 941 documents 54/100 Counties we could measure at all 46 yielded nothing 33.4% Are pictures of text need OCR, not tagging 0 Median score out of 100 The deadline has not passed, and that is the point. On 20 April 2026 the DOJ extended ADA Title II compliance to 26 April 2027 for entities serving 50,000 or more people, and 26 April 2028 for smaller ones. There is still time. But the rule’s exception for documents posted _before_ the compliance date does not cover documents people currently use to apply for, access, or take part in a service, and that describes most of what a county publishes: permit applications, tax forms, benefit paperwork, meeting agendas. Retagging a back catalogue takes months, not weeks. A county that starts the week before the deadline has already missed it. “An untagged permit form is not a hardtoread document. It is a blank page with a mouseonly signature box.” Key findings 1\. Untagged is the norm, not the exception. 58.1% of the 941 documents we could assess have no document structure tree. Weighted by county rather than by document, the average county’s untagged rate is 57%. Both numbers are reported because they answer different questions: the first is what a resident encounters, the second is what a typical county publishes. 2\. Size does not predict this. Counties in the smallest population fifth had an untagged rate of 59.3%, against 49.7% in the largest fifth. That looks like a gradient until you read the middle: the second fifth is the worst in the study at 72.1%, above both ends, on 7 counties. With so few counties behind each band there is no reliable trend here, and we are not going to claim one. What the bands do show is that no size of county is in good shape, including the largest, which face the earlier 26 April 2027 deadline. 3\. The failures cluster on structure, not on decoration. WCAG 1.3.1 failed in 98.9% of documents. These are not cosmetic complaints: they are the criteria that decide whether assistive technology can determine what a piece of content _is_. A document can look immaculate on screen and still fail every one of them. 4\. Some documents cannot be fixed by tagging at all. 33.4% of the documents are pictures of text: scanned paper with no characters in the file. Tagging cannot help them, because there is nothing to tag. They need OCR first, which is a different budget line and a different vendor conversation, and we report them separately for that reason rather than folding them into the untagged number. How counties are spread Share of each county's sampled documents that have no tag tree, across the 54 counties that yielded documents. None untagged1 county Under a quarter0 counties A quarter to half19 counties Half to three quarters21 counties Three quarters or more, not all11 counties Every document untagged2 counties By population band Counties sorted by population and split into five equalcount fifths. Scores exclude colour contrast, so they are not comparable with a customer report. __Untagged rate and mean score by county population band__ Population band Counties Documents Untagged Mean score Smallest fifth 13 214 59.3% 23.1 Second fifth 7 136 72.1% 13.9 Middle fifth 11 205 58.5% 21.6 Fourth fifth 11 201 54.7% 18.8 Largest fifth 12 185 49.7% 23.7 Mostfailed WCAG criteria Counted once per document, not per occurrence, so a single enormous document cannot dominate. WCAG 1.3.1931 docs98.9% WCAG 1.3.2889 docs94.5% WCAG 1.1.1470 docs49.9% WCAG 3.1.1288 docs30.6% WCAG 3.1.2288 docs30.6% WCAG 4.1.272 docs7.7% WCAG 2.4.628 docs3% What we could not measure Reachability is a finding of this study, not a footnote. Every county we could not measure is listed here with the reason. __Counties that yielded no documents, by reason__ Reason Counties Blocked by bot protection we did not bypass 19 Portal did not respond 9 No public county portal exists 7 No PDFs found within the crawl's limits 4 Documents found, but none would download 2 Ratelimited too heavily to measure 2 robots.txt refused us 2 Portal returned an error 1 21 counties sat behind bot protection or rate limiting we chose not to defeat. Blocking is not spread evenly across the sample: 0 of the 20 smallest counties were blocked, against 21 of the other 80. We report that split without drawing a conclusion from it. It is tempting to argue that bot protection costs money and therefore hides betterresourced counties, which would mean these figures flatter the sector, but the pattern across the bands is not orderly enough to support the claim in either direction, and a guess about the counties we could not see is exactly the kind of thing this study should not be making. Check one of your own PDFs Run the same PDF/UA check we used for this study, free, no signup. You will see whether the document has a tag tree, which WCAG criteria it fails, and what a repair would actually change. [Check a PDF free](/pdfaccessibilitychecker) Methodology Sampling This is a probability sample, not a curated list. We sorted all 3,144 US county and countyequivalent governments by Census population estimate, split them into five equalcount bands, and drew 20 counties per band with a fixed seed, giving 100 counties. Equal counts per band, not equal populations, because the question is whether county size predicts anything, which needs comparable sample sizes rather than comparable populations. items.descZh: 美国所有县须在 2027 年 4 月 26 日前完成 ADA Title II 数字无障碍合规。研究团队按人口五等分抽样 100 个县，从公开门户抓取 941 份 PDF 检测其 PDF/UA 结构，58.1%（547 份）完全无标签树，屏幕阅读器无法获取标题、阅读顺序与表格结构；54 个县产出有效数据，另 46 个因反爬或无门户无法测量。中位无障碍得分仅 0/100，33.4% 的文件本质是图片化文字（需 OCR 而非标签修复），98.9% 文件未通过 WCAG 1.3.1。核心功能是面向公众的免费 PDF 无障碍检测工具，可即时返回标签树状态、失败准则与修复建议。亮点是按文件与按县加权分别报告 58.1% 与 57% 的无标签率，并诚实披露第二五分位（72.1%）反而最差、强调小样本下不作趋势结论的反例设计。该工具适用于 2027/2028 截止日前做存量回溯的县政府法务、IT 与无障碍合规团队，尤其针对申请表、税务与福利表单等"现役"关键文档优先修复。
